description:
Description: Combining the digital and the real world will be key to address the mega-challenges ahead of our society. Sufficiently accurate and fast digital models of assets, products, systems, and infrastructures are required to do so. This will only be achieved in the remaining time frame by tightly integrating machine learning and physics-based methods (hybrid digital twins).
 
In this context, we highlight industrial challenges from design & engineering up to operations of complex industrial systems. Along selected deep dives we demonstrate how hybrid digital twins achieve the right model accuracy and speed without requiring significant manual expert efforts. The latter is today one of the main limiting factors for realization of more digital twins.  Finally, we will indicate fields requiring more research from an industrial point of view in the field of computational science & engineering and machine learning.

Bio: Dirk Hartmann is an industrial mathematician, Siemens Technical Fellow, intrapreneur, and thought leader in the field of Simulation and Digital Twin. Among many distinctions, he received the prestigious Werner-von-Siemens Top Innovator award for his life-time achievements and the Siemens Inventor of the Year 2021. Multiple of his innovations have led to novel products and services, have been showcased at top-level innovation events, as well as have been covered by external media.
 
In his career, Dirk Hartmann took several leading roles in research, innovation, and development across Siemens including the lead of a multi-million Siemens R&D program and the technical leadership for the Simulation & Digital Twin field at Siemens Technology with more than 120 scientists across the globe. He is a passionate mentor, teacher, and supervisor for the next generation of innovators and experts exploring novel Digital Twin solutions for all industries.
